title.rendered: The stock market has taken a heavy hit in recent weeks. Trump is blaming the Democrats for it: ‘It will only get worse’

content.rendered:
President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to pin the recent stock market slide on Democrats. He argued that the drop began right after the party’s midterm results earlier this month and said their approach is the sole cause.

In the post, Trump wrote, “The Market is down more than 6 Trillion Dollars since the Democrats’ rather strange ‘win’ on November 3rd. NASDAQ, by itself, is down 20%.” He followed that with a direct assessment of the party’s priorities.

He stated, “This is 100% due to the fact that the Democrats are ‘BAD’ due to their Anti Growth, and Retribution Only, Policies, and worse. If they don’t change, FAST, it will only get worse.” Trump closed the message by adding, “But fear not, our Country will soon be STRONG AGAIN – Lots of good things happening!”

Declines across major indexes accelerate through November trading

According to Mediaite, measured from the close on November 2, the day before the midterm results, the three leading indexes have all posted clear losses. The Nasdaq has fallen 10.1 percent. The S&P 500 is down 8.4 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average has dropped 7.4 percent.

Friday produced the sharpest session of the stretch. The S&P 500 lost 3.7 percent, marking its largest single-day decline in 18 months. The Nasdaq fell 5.3 percent in the same session as technology stocks saw a massive surge in selling.

The retreat in artificial intelligence stocks has been a central feature of the move lower. Some analysts have connected that weakness to statements from Democratic lawmakers who have expressed opposition to new data centers.

Nvidia faced an additional setback of its own. Founder Jensen Huang was removed after allegations of an affair involving a person described as a suspected Chinese spy. Trump, however, wants him back.

The indexes had climbed between 13 percent and 20.4 percent during 2025. Following the November selling, the Nasdaq and the Dow Jones now sit below their opening levels for the year, while the S&P 500 remains up roughly 0.5 percent year to date.

Throughout his second term, Trump has often highlighted the stock market as evidence of progress. The latest declines have erased a portion of those earlier advances.

title.rendered: Amazon warns NYC customers that delivery could soon cost $5 more. Then Mayor Mamdani responds to the red ‘attention’ banner: ‘It’s greed’

content.rendered:
Amazon is pushing back hard against a new piece of legislation in New York City, and they are using their own platform to rally customers to the cause, HuffPost reports. On Thursday, shoppers in the city noticed a red attention banner at the top of the Amazon website and app. The warning states that the NYC Council could add up to 5 dollars per order if a specific bill passes. This move marks a major shift in the ongoing conflict between the retail giant and city leadership.

The bill in question is known as the Delivery Protection Act. It aims to force Amazon to directly hire the drivers who handle their local deliveries. Right now, Amazon uses a system where they outsource this work to smaller firms they call delivery service partners. While Amazon claims this model helps small businesses grow, it has drawn heavy criticism from labor unions and city officials. Critics argue that this setup lets the company avoid legal liabilities and keeps working conditions lower than they should be.

The legislation would require companies to employ drivers directly if they want to move packages from city facilities. This change would not only impact Amazon but could also force other logistics companies like FedEx to change how they operate.

If the act becomes law, it would effectively break the current delivery service partner system in the city

Julie Su, the deputy mayor for economic justice, has been vocal about this topic. She noted in September that such outsourcing practices have spread throughout the economy, which makes jobs less secure. She said the direct hire mandate is intended to make corporations more accountable for things like driver safety.

Amazon is not taking this lightly. The company claims that if the bill passes, it would put its delivery service partners out of business. They have even threatened to move their delivery hubs out of New York City entirely. If that happened, drivers would need to pick up packages in New Jersey or Connecticut, which would mean longer delivery times for residents.

The 5 dollar cost estimate mentioned in the app banners comes from an analysis by a consulting group for the Five Borough Jobs Campaign. This is a business coalition that has received funding from Amazon and is currently running ads against the bill.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani did not hold back when he saw the messages from Amazon on X. He pointed out that the company is a multi-trillion-dollar entity. He said, “If Jeff Bezos adds $5 to your order, it’s not because of City Council’s efforts to protect workers’ rights and keep our streets safe. It’s greed.”

The company says their campaign has already generated 60,000 emails to the city council as of Friday afternoon. Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel stated that the company wants to be transparent with customers about potential costs. She said, “As the City Council continues to review this bill, we want to be transparent with our customers about what it would cost them if it passes as written — which is why we’re doing this.”

She added that they remain hopeful the bill will not pass as it is currently written. Amazon has invited council members to visit their delivery hubs to speak with the owners of their partner firms, though they report that not many have taken them up on that offer. Nantel said, “We continue urging them to do so, and hope they’ll be willing to work with us.”

title.rendered: Trump shares a lengthy list of accomplishments on Truth Social, and claims he ‘defeated inflation inherited from the Biden administration’

content.rendered:
President Donald Trump spent part of Sunday posting on Truth Social, and one of the messages was a detailed rundown of what he described as major successes. The entry carried the heading “Wins of President Trump.” Earlier in the day, he had also passed along positive remarks from supporters and pointed to Democrats as the reason for a recent drop in the stock market.

The list itself ran through a wide range of topics. Trump wrote that he had achieved net deregulation and ended DEI. He also stated that he had “ended transgender insanity,” along with claims that the border was fully secured and that deportations had reached record levels.

Other points on the same post asserted that crime and the murder rate had both fallen to record lows. The list further noted record production of American fossil fuels and of American coal, and said the first nuclear reactors had gone critical since the 1970s.

Trump made some disputable claims in his post

Trump’s post continued with additional items. It said global trade had been rebalanced and that the military had been rebuilt. The list also claimed the entire federal law enforcement apparatus had been rebuilt and that drug cartels had been confronted with lethal force for the first time in American history.

One entry stated that Venezuela had been taken over in less than an hour, an action the post said doubled U.S. oil reserves. Democrats, however, plan to look into the $100 billion deal Trump signed with the South American country.

Trump brought up “reformed relationships with Russia and China” as well. Recently, he attended a historic trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. But no major breakthroughs were achieved regarding ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. Separate lines mentioned a strong economy and the fastest wage growth.

The final claim on the list was that Trump had “defeated inflation inherited from the Biden administration.” Mediaite points out that this statement does not address the war in Iran or the large rise in gas and diesel prices that followed. Those higher fuel costs raise the price of groceries and other goods by increasing what it costs to transport them.

According to data from Macro Trends, the annual inflation rate in 2025, the first year of Trump’s second term, was 2.68 percent. That was only slightly below the 2.89 percent rate recorded in 2024, President Joe Biden’s last year in office. The rate moved higher again in 2026 once the Iran War started in February. It now stands at 4.15 percent.

On crime, the information indicates the country is currently seeing record-low crime and murder rates. Mediaite, however, highlights that the decline is continuing a multi-year pattern that was already underway before the present administration took office.

title.rendered: Review: ‘Focker In-Law’ is a safe and predictable sequel with  a popstar-shaped problem

content.rendered:
It has been 16 long years since we last spent time with the Fockers. But, despite the critical mauling of 2010’s Little Fockers, the franchise grossing over a billion dollars over three movies meant its eventual return was an inevitability.

A quarter century has passed since Meet the Parents, and we return to the Fockers franchise to find it locked in comedy stasis and firmly in ‘playing the hits’ mode. Back in 2000, audiences clutched their sides as Ben Stiller’s hapless nurse Greg Focker descended on Robert De Niro’s former CIA officer Jack Bynes’ home. There was the iconic lie detector interrogation, mishaps involving a beloved family member’s ashes, a family pet wreaking havoc, and a series of farcical misunderstandings with a heartwarming ending.

All of the above also happens in Focker-in-Law, giving the entire film a strange atmosphere of deja vu. But hey, if it’s not broke, don’t fix it, right?

As before, so again

This time, the core drama revolves around Greg Focker’s son Henry (Skyler Gisondo), who is bringing the love of his life Olivia (Ariana Grande) to… Meet the Parents (also the grandparents). That’s happening against the backdrop of Jack Bynes 80th birthday celebrations, which means the cast is once again descending on their leafy Long Island home. Incidentally, Bynes appears to have gotten over his life-threatening heart condition that was at the core of Little Fockers and is now a supernaturally strong vegan fitness fanatic.

Let’s get one thing clear up top. Focker In-Law is not a disaster. If a comedy makes me laugh out loud at least three times it is, on some level, a success. Stiller and De Niro remain an amusing classic comedy double act of fool and straight man, and they’re ably assisted by a very funny supporting cast including Owen Wilson (still doing his thing, and doing it well), Beanie Feinstein, and Eduardo Franco.

But there’s a popstar-shaped fly in this ointment. On paper, Ariana Grande should be a good fit for this franchise. After all, she made her name in Nickelodeon teen sitcoms Victorious and Sam & Cat, both domestic farces centered on comedic domestic misunderstandings that share obvious territory with the Fockers franchise.

Grande was great in those, so why can’t she just dust off her old Nickelodeon skills a decade and change later? Grande can act, has good chemistry with her co-stars, and most crucially, she is funny. But she is also Ariana Grande and, in 2026, sticks out like a sore thumb in a domestic family comedy drama.

Focker In-Law introduces Grande’s Olivia as a Californian life coach, which feels in her wheelhouse. Then, early on, it’s revealed that she’s actually spent six years as an FBI hostage negotiator. Grande was eminently plausible as the ethereal Glinda the Good, but as a hard-bitten FBI veteran? It just doesn’t scan.

The script attempts to hang a lantern on this by having Stiller say Olivia isn’t what he expected an FBI hostage negotiator to look like. Olivia counters that her appearance not conforming with expectations is what made her a good hostage negotiator (an argument slightly undermined by hostage negotiators not generally coming face-to-face with those they’re negotiating with, but whatever). But she is just not believable as an FBI veteran.

Grande is also impeccably turned out throughout, looking elegant, beautiful, and groomed to nanometer perfection in every shot (special credit to whoever was in charge of eyelash-fluffing duty). But, as great as she looks, having her walk into a room full of wrinkly, rumpled, and generally ordinary-looking characters makes her look like an ethereal being descended from the stars rather than “nervous girlfriend of son meeting the family.” She does her best with the material she’s given and I can’t fault her performance, but at no point does Ariana Grande feel like she has any business being in a Fockers movie.

Focker In-Law ends, as we somehow knew it must, with the tease of another film to come. After all, Ariana Grande’s character also has parents to meet and you can bet they’ll be eccentric! Somehow I suspect this dangling plot thread won’t be resolved, as I imagine Grande will have better things to do than return for Fockers 5.

If you have fond memories of Meet the Parents and want to see that done again but not as good, Focker In-Law is the movie for you. It’s a painfully safe movie with any sharp edges filed away and zero surprises, but it did make me laugh a few times. It could be worse!

The reviewer attended a public preview screening of the movie and paid for his own ticket.

title.rendered: Trump stands with Vance and Rubio at press conference. Then he points to Stephen Miller and names his favorite for 2028: ‘Better than these two guys’

content.rendered:
Donald Trump certainly knows how to keep everyone on their toes, and he just did it again at a White House press conference in Washington on Friday. He pointed right at his new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, and called him a possible contender for the 2028 US presidential election, saying he was “better than these two guys” while looking at Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

This whole exchange happened after Miller’s promotion earlier in November from deputy chief of staff, a move that came after Republican losses in the midterm elections. That appointment definitely got some lawmakers talking, mainly because of Miller’s strong immigration policies, which have been a big part of his work in Trump’s administration.

When Trump invited Miller to speak at the podium, Miller promised to make the rest of Trump’s presidency the “greatest two years in American history.” Trump then really laid on the praise, calling Miller the “most powerful man in the world” and even asking him if he wanted to run for president. After hearing Miller speak, Trump turned to Vance and Rubio and made that direct comparison, calling Miller “better than these two guys.”

Miller didn’t actually answer the question about running, though

Trump also didn’t announce a preferred successor or say anything about what role Miller might play in the next presidential campaign. So, his intentions for the election are still up in the air. This public comparison, however, definitely puts Miller right up there with two senior officials who are already getting a lot of attention as possible successors to Trump. It also comes after some reported tensions involving the vice president.

Vance has long been considered a potential heir to Trump’s political movement, but his position has been under fresh scrutiny since the midterm elections. This is especially true after he criticized the political consequences of the Iran war. After the Republican defeat, Vance posted a long statement blaming the conflict for the party’s losses.

Reports suggested Trump had grown frustrated with Vance’s remarks, though Trump denied being unhappy with the statement at Friday’s press conference. Trump later removed Vance from talks about Iran and told him to give his “complete and total attention” to allegations of corruption in Democratic-run states.

This shift definitely added to questions about how the vice president would handle his relationship with Trump while thinking about a presidential campaign. Vance has said he will decide “sometime next year” whether to run, indicating in a Fox News interview aired on November 16 that he was in no rush and didn’t want to set a firm deadline.

Rubio has also emerged as a possible rival to Vance. Republican operatives and donors have reportedly encouraged the secretary of state to seek the 2028 nomination, positioning him as a potential alternative to Vance. While this shows some pressure, it doesn’t mean Rubio has decided to enter the race.

Rubio recently stood next to Trump during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and greeted Russian President Vladimir Putin during another encounter involving the US president. His high visibility at both meetings came before Trump’s favorable comments about him in the Philippines.

At a Tuesday dinner hosted by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, Trump asked ASEAN leaders, “How hot is Marco, right?” He added, “Is Marco doing a great job? He’s been fantastic.”
